newsitem.title: GERMANY: German trade fair company looking for partners. [CORRECTED 17:51 GMT]
newsitem.headline: German trade fair company looking for partners. [CORRECTED 17:51 GMT]

text.p: German trade fair company Messe Frankfurt GmbH said on Wednesday it was interested in forming partnerships with other congress centre businesses.
"Discussion of strategic alliances among the large German congress centres should no longer be a taboo topic," Eike Markau, chief executive of the Messe Frankfurt, told journalists.
"That is especially true in our foreign trade fair business." Markau said.

Markau said the company's need for powerful partners was linked to the increasing globalisation and concentration of business and would help it hold its own among publicly-listed and private competitors abroad.

He said he was satisfied with the previous business year, although the company had posted a slight drop in revenues from the previous year. Profits reached 17 million marks ($9.3 million) in 1996, down from 18.1 million marks in the previous year.
Turnover also dropped to 377.5 million marks from 427.6 million marks.
Markau said he was particulary pleased with growth among the company's units in Tokyo, Hong Kong, Singapore and Atlanta.

Business abroad currently represents 6.5 percent of Messe Frankfurt turnover, Markau said, and he predicted the figure would jump to 20 percent in the coming yearst. (Corrects time frame for increase.)
